topic: general-purpose frontier language models playing chess in recent GothamChess videos

source_policy.reason: Creator videos and transcripts are not an approved training corpus. Only identifiers, public metadata, short derived observations, and benchmark hypotheses are versioned.

collection.initial_discovery_method: vidIQ channel-video search and transcript inspection
collection.notes: The repository helper intentionally cannot download media or subtitles. Its normalized output is written under data/private/, which is ignored by git.

videos.title: GPT-6, GPT-6.1, ORION 1 & KURO 4.7 FIGHT FOR THE TITLE!
GPT-6.1 IS PROBABLY THE BEST CHESS AI EVER
GPT-6.1 VS GPT-6 ASTRA: CHESS AI FIGHT FOR GLORY

derived_observations.observation: The showcased agents can produce stretches of coherent legal and tactically relevant play despite not being presented as chess-specialized models.
The videos are not controlled model evaluations: model interfaces, prompts, legal-move handling, opening familiarity, time or token budgets, and repeat counts are not held constant.
derived_observations.evidence_scope: format and procedures visible in the three videos

derived_observations.observation: At least one showcased interaction includes an illegal or rejected move path, illustrating that board-state tracking and interface compliance must be measured separately from move quality.
Informal strength estimates and single-game outcomes are insufficient for calibrated Elo or for claims about explanation faithfulness.

benchmark_implications: Keep general-purpose frontier models only as observational controls, not the planned production route.
Compare chess-specialized models under identical representations, prompts, compute limits, and seeds.
Measure raw legality before applying a legality mask, then report masked move quality separately.
Score board-state understanding, move policy, and commentary factuality as separate capabilities.
Use clustered repeated positions and games; do not infer strength from a single exhibition game.
Retain the repository's no-forward-input commentary gate so engine answers cannot leak into generation.
